title: Optimistic updates with revision checks
summary: Compute a candidate outside the lock and commit it only if the snapshot revision still matches.
code: raise RuntimeError("update conflicted too many times")
triggers: optimistic concurrency control and lost updates
compare a revision after work outside a critical section
prompts: Recompute a shared setting outside its mutex and merge concurrent edits by retrying from a fresh snapshot.
Reject a stale commit even when the value changed and then returned to its original value.
invariant: The value and revision are read and committed together under the same lock. Every accepted commit advances the revision, even if the value is unchanged.
mantra: Read a revision, compute, validate before writing.
pitfalls: Keep snapshot values immutable. Mutating a shared object outside the lock would bypass revision checks.
A retry can call the transform again. Keep side effects outside the transform.
With sustained contention a caller can exhaust its attempts. Short serialized updates may cost less than repeating expensive work.

mutations.explanation: Fetching a fresh revision without recomputing the candidate lets a stale write overwrite a newer update.

test: jobs = [pool.submit(update, counter, increment) for _ in range(2)]
assert sorted(job.result(timeout=3) for job in jobs) == [1, 2]
raise AssertionError("Expected the retry limit to be reached")
